independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The assumptions include n=1 and Section9 explicitly claims any space dimension. The actual recursively defined z_v is the arithmetic average of normalized cell densities. On [0,epsilon] and [epsilon,1], the continuous quadratic bump 6(x/epsilon)(1-x/epsilon) on the short cell has vertex-average coefficients 1,1/2,0. Root independently integrated the resulting piecewise-linear W0: input norm squared 6*epsilon/5 and output (1+6*epsilon)/12, hence ratio 5(1+6*epsilon)/(72*epsilon) diverges while the source-defined shape constant is exactly1. The input has zero endpoint traces and fixed degree2. This refutes the central shape-only uniform stability claim in its admitted dimension; fixed-mesh boundedness, n>=2 and algebraic identities are not refuted.

A boundary vertex of one triangle has a one-edge ball link with incidence (-1,1). The actual beta in (3.8) requires the unique primitive mu=(lambda_b-lambda_a)/2, generally nonzero, while the terminal orientation functional (2.9) requires plus-or-minus mu=0. The earlier sentence calling the boundary arrow redundant is genuine counterevidence for an intended omission, but (3.8) explicitly reimposes (2.9) in link dimension1. A clear boundary convention deleting/zeroing only the ball-link terminal map repairs this. The sphere-link map and separate relative zero-trace terminal integral are retained.

The exterior derivative display lacks alternating signs and can fail to be alternating. Link dimension n-m is zero at m=n, not n-1. Lemma4.4's proof needs j<n-m, consistent with its induction, rather than the impossible j<m-n. Equation(5.4) needs target degree k-j-1, already given in the immediately preceding definition. These have local determined repairs; no additional central failures are inferred.

findings.title: The terminal link gauge must distinguish boundary links from closed links
findings.claim_checked: For every allowed link, a chain cycle has a primitive uniquely selected by delta_(k+1) primitive=0, including the nonzero top functional(2.9) when n-m=1.
findings.counterexample: Take Omega to be a single nondegenerate triangle in R^2 and f one boundary vertex. The link is the single oriented edge e=[a,b]. In the bases (a,b) and e, partial_1=(-1,1)^T and partial_0=(1,1). The cycle c=(-1,1) has only the primitive e, while delta_1 e=+1 or -1 by(2.9). Consequently the required terminal gauge is impossible. The actual Section3/4 data are beta_a=(lambda_a-lambda_b)/2 and beta_b=-beta_a, with forced primitive mu_e=(lambda_b-lambda_a)/2. Its terminal value is nonzero as a polynomial for either orientation; at barycentric coordinates (1/2,1/3,1/6), mu_e=-1/12.
findings.logical_consequence: The displayed augmented sequence is not even a complex on this interval if the printed terminal functional is retained: delta_1 delta_0(0,1)=+1 or -1. The printed recursion therefore fails on an admitted boundary mesh. This is not an OCR-based finding: both(2.9) and the explicit instruction beneath(3.8) were actually viewed.
findings.counterevidence_and_scope: The paper already says the last arrow may be redundant for boundary links, indicating the likely intended convention. For a closed sphere link, the augmented terminal functional is appropriate and fixes the top primitive's harmonic ambiguity. The obstruction is local to applying that nonzero functional to a ball link. No counterexample to a correctly specified bubble transform is claimed.
findings.repair: When the actual link f* is a ball with boundary, use its ordinary augmented cochain complex ending C_q -> 0, equivalently set its terminal delta_q to zero; retain the top functional for a closed sphere link. Specify this in Lemma2.1,(3.8), and the coefficient gauges(4.7). A boundary simplex here means one whose link has boundary, not merely a simplex with some boundary vertices. For a ball link partial_q is injective, so the top primitive is already unique. Then partial beta_q=0 forces beta_q=0. The separate relative full-zero-trace complex on Omega_f must retain its terminal integral.
findings.repair_check: With delta_1=0 the triangle primitive exists uniquely, and rho dmu-mu d rho=lambda_a d lambda_b-lambda_b d lambda_a=phi_ab, so beta_edge=0 as required. In the later(4.13) compatibility, range(delta_(q-1)) is all top cochains on a ball. No later Section4-5 use was found that imposes the discarded terminal link condition. The full corrected theorem has not been independently certified.
findings.impact_judgment: Minor: the literal construction has a real missing boundary convention, but the identified correction is local and no remaining obstruction appears in the checked recursion and order-reduction arguments. It must be propagated explicitly. This bounded severity does not assess the separate shape-only stability failure owned by the other helper.

findings.title: Two local range and form-degree corrections
details: The proof's condition 0<=j<m-n should read 0<=j<n-m, as required by the immediately preceding case split and Corollary4.2.
The target form degree in(5.4) should be k-j-1, consistent with the Q definition and the sentence immediately above. The parameter degree index r is unchanged.

positive_checks.check: Mesh, topology, ranges, and theorem context
positive_checks.reasoning: The local analysis uses links of nonempty simplices and stars, not global contractibility of Omega. A finite conforming triangulation of a polyhedral Lipschitz domain permits the single-triangle boundary witness. For f of dimension m-1 the link has dimension q=n-m. Interior links have sphere topology and boundary links have ball topology; the ordinary boundary-link cochain complex and the full-zero-trace differential-form complex on Omega_f must be distinguished. No n>=2 restriction is stated in the assumptions. Theorem2.3 gives support on Omega_f; top-dimensional bubbles may depend on the extended macroelement. The separate 1D stability issue is owned by the other native helper and parent.

positive_checks.check: Inductive beta cancellation, conditional on a correct link primitive convention
positive_checks.reasoning: Write rho=rho_f. Assuming partial mu_j=beta_(j-1), applying partial to beta_j and commuting the spatial derivative with the chain operator gives partial beta_j=(-1)^(j-1)[rho^(j+1)d(phi_(j-1)/rho^j)-partial phi_j]. Whitney identity(2.5), summed over link vertices and using rho=sum lambda_i on Omega_f, makes the bracket zero. This calculation is valid where rho>0; polynomial formula(4.2) extends it through rho=0, so the quotient notation does not introduce an actual singularity into beta. The next primitive exists under the correctly chosen sphere/ball cochain complex. The boundary terminal gauge in the printed text is separately flagged.

For m=n the link has one boundary vertex or two interior vertices. The authors treat this separately: mu_vertex=-1/|f*|, beta_vertex=lambda_vertex-rho_f/|f*|, and sum beta_vertex=0. No unavailable next edge primitive is required. The coefficient formulation is the Whitney expansion of partial mu=beta; its terminal gauge needs the same boundary correction. Expanding rho_g^(j+1)d(mu/rho_g^j)=rho_g dmu-j d rho_g wedge mu and subtracting the corresponding rho_f formula gives(4.9) with psi from(4.8). The j=0 formula reduces to (rho_g-rho_f)/|f*| and is consistent with the augmented convention.

delta^+ removes an e-vertex and inserts it into f; transferring two vertices in opposite orders changes the incidence sign, yielding (delta^+)^2=0. Removing one vertex and transferring another gives delta delta^+=-delta^+ delta. Formula(4.14) uses weights already defined on larger simplices, so the m-recursion is descending and not circular. At j=-1 it gives the stated average of top-form weights. Each support Omega_<xi,f> lies in Omega_f and each weight has full zero trace on its own macroelement boundary; extension by zero preserves the required full boundary trace. The proof explicitly distinguishes this from mere support, which is insufficient at a boundary simplex.

positive_checks.check: Top recursion compatibility and differential identity
positive_checks.reasoning: The compatibility of the right side of(4.16) follows by pairing partial beta=0 with delta^+dw in range(delta). The base case interprets the derivative of a top form as its integral and uses the normalized value -1. This is the relative complex on Omega_f with full boundary trace; its terminal integral must remain even when a link is a ball. For a boundary ball link, range(delta_(q-1)) is all top cochains and partial_q is injective, so beta_q=0 after the corrected primitive construction. No later step checked here needs a nonzero terminal link functional imposed on mu. Lemma4.4 then follows from partial beta=0, the anticommutation of delta and delta^+, and(4.14). Its printed j<m-n range is a local typo; the surrounding induction and proof require j<n-m.

positive_checks.check: Weight support, d relation, and tensor transfer identity
positive_checks.reasoning: With z=delta^+w, the complex identity gives delta^+z=0. Combining dw=(-1)^(j+1)(delta w-delta^+w), with the appropriate shifted j in delta^+w, and delta^+delta=-delta delta^+ gives dz=(-1)^(j+1)delta z. The support is the union over i in e of Omega_f intersect Omega_xi, namely Omega_f intersect Omega_e^E. Full zero trace on boundary Omega passes from w to z. In Lemma4.6, reindexing the transferred vertex turns phi_e into phi_[xi,e]; identity(2.5) and(4.14) reproduce the same sum on the psi side. No extra topological hypothesis or boundary integral is used in that tensor identity.

positive_checks.check: Graded Stokes signs for R and Q
positive_checks.reasoning: For alpha=Pi_(j-1)G_f^*u of y-degree j-1, full zero trace gives integral d_y alpha wedge z=(-1)^j integral alpha wedge dz. Substituting dz=(-1)^(j+1)delta z contributes -delta R. Together with d_y Pi_(j-1)G^*u+(-1)^j d_S Pi_jG^*u=Pi_jG^*du this yields R^(k+1)du=(-1)^j dR^k u-delta R^k u, exactly(2.18). For Q, alpha=Pi_jG^*u has y-degree j. The outer factor(-1)^(j+1) cancels the Stokes sign, leaving integral Pi_jG^*u wedge dw. Inserting(4.16) proves Lemma5.2. The endpoint j=k is handled by the same product identity with Pi_(k+1)G^*u=0; the identity is elementary beyond the shortened printed range in(5.1). These checks use the conventional exterior derivative, whose missing sign in an earlier displayed definition is handled by the parent.

Intermediate expressions compare R operators associated to different f, whose parameter simplices differ. Their meaningful common restriction is S_g: embed it in S_f by setting the extra coordinates to zero. Then G_f(y,lambda)=G_g(y,lambda) and the tangent derivatives agree on S_g for every f containing g. Thus the coefficient identity from Lemma4.6 passes to the claimed L_g^*R identity. The same restriction explains delta^+Q=R and delta^+R=0. The final stated identities are well-defined with these natural restrictions; no failure of the final identity is inferred from abbreviated intermediate notation.

positive_checks.check: Degree, smooth extension, and ordinary polynomial mapping
positive_checks.reasoning: A q-y-slot component of G_f^*u has exactly q factors b because D_yG_f=b I. Dividing by b^q therefore removes an algebraic factor and gives a smooth extension through b=0. For y in a source simplex containing f, G_f(y,lambda) remains in that same simplex, so piecewise polynomial coefficients may be integrated on fixed cells. After division, their parameter degree is at most r. For R, q=j and output form degree is k-j. For Q, q=j+1 and output degree is k-j-1; it is zero for k<j+1. Thus(5.4)'s target degree k is incorrect, but its intended reduced degree is stated immediately above. The general historical proofs in[7] were not acquired or reread by this helper; the present direct algebra covers the normalized polynomial factor and the supplemental trimmed argument below.

positive_checks.check: Supplemental trimmed-polynomial cancellation: general analytic proof
positive_checks.reasoning: Let X=x be a radial vector field in fixed affine coordinates on a target simplex, and let u_r be the homogeneous coefficient-degree-r part of u in P_r^-Lambda^k. The standard defining characterization is i_X u_r=0 (for k=0 this condition is automatic). On each source and target simplex, G_f(y,L_g x)=a_g(y)+B_g(y)x. In the normalized q-y-slot operator T_q, b^q cancels exactly, the y-slots are placed first, and the remaining x-slots are B_g(y)v. Hence the coefficient-degree-r part of T_q^k u is obtained from u_r(B_g(y)x). It satisfies i_X(T_q^k u)_r=0. Cartan's identity gives i_Y d u_r=(r+k)u_r for Y at the source point, since u_r is homogeneous and i_Yu_r=0. Inserting B_g(y)x after q y-slots contributes (-1)^q, so i_X(T_q^(k+1)du)_(r-1)=(-1)^q(r+k)(T_q^k u)_r. These identities hold before integration and hence after integration against the fixed weight.
positive_checks.continuation: Each summand in the displayed representation has H^k u=eta wedge T_q^k u, with eta a Whitney form of degree q-1: eta=mu_e for R with q=j, or eta=phi_e for Q with q=j+1. Its homogeneous coefficient-degree-one part eta_1 satisfies i_Xeta_1=0. Thus H_top=eta_1 wedge(T_q^k u)_r has coefficient degree r+1, form degree k-1, and i_XH_top=0. Cartan gives i_XdH_top=(r+k)H_top. On the other hand, the wedge contraction sign gives i_X(eta_1 wedge(T_q^(k+1)du)_(r-1))=(-1)^(q-1)(-1)^q(r+k)H_top=-(r+k)H_top. The two contractions cancel in dH+Hd. Both terms have coefficient degree at most r, and the degree-r part is annihilated by i_X, so their sum is in P_r^-Lambda^k. When q=k+1, H^k=0 and the remaining leading term eta_1 times a scalar is already annihilated by i_X; for q>k+1 both terms vanish. For k=0 only the ordinary polynomial degree bound is needed. This closes the general trimmed argument conditional on correctly defined weights. The actual PDF37 image confirms the common factor(-1)^j applies to the entire Q[dH+Hd] bracket, so it does not disturb the cancellation.
positive_checks.counterevidence_to_initial_concern: The cited wedge inclusion alone does not explain a term-by-term index reduction: d(P_r^-Lambda^k) is generally ordinary P_(r-1)Lambda^(k+1), not trimmed P_(r-1)^-. The initial concern is resolved by the cancellation just proved, not by assuming a stronger mapping theorem from[7]. The parent's separate exact two-triangle r=1 test is not executed or relabeled here.

coverage.boundary_cases: Single-triangle boundary link gives the material definition finding; zero-dimensional links and high form-degree zero operators checked. Parent/other helper own the n=1 uniform stability failure.
coverage.counterevidence: The redundant-arrow sentence and a precise boundary repair were explicitly considered. The initially incomplete termwise polynomial-degree argument was resolved by a new general cancellation proof. No unsupported stronger mapping theorem or software failure is asserted.
coverage.additional_domain_caveat: The displayed d_f^* map(4.12) need not, literally, send every full-zero-trace form to a full-zero-trace form at boundary f if it sums all g containing f. On a square triangulated by its diagonal [f,c], with f a boundary endpoint, the interior-edge Whitney form phi_[f,c] has zero boundary trace, but the formula produces a nonzero multiple of the boundary-vertex hat phi_f. A true adjoint on the relative subcomplex should project to its admissible coefficient space. No separate defect is rated here: the construction imposes this gauge at form degree dim f, where the displayed sum over lower-dimensional g containing f is empty, and no necessary failed later solve was established.
coverage.scope_limits: No numerical performance claim, author implementation, or new experiment is present in Sections4-5. No missing-code defect is alleged. The full corrected theorem and all stability constants were not certified by this child.

checks.claim: The uniform stability claim is tied to n and the stated shape constant, with different dependence domains for proper-face and top-cell bubbles.
checks.reasoning: Section 2.1 assumes a bounded polyhedral Lipschitz domain in R^n and a finite conforming simplicial decomposition. No n>=2 restriction appears there. Theorem 2.3 includes 0<=k<=n and refers to Proposition 8.1 for stable decomposition. Section 8 defines c_T=max_T diam(T)/diam(B_T), explicitly allows constants also to depend on n, and claims uniformity for mesh families with bounded c_T. Proper-face B_f has input/output patch Omega_f, whereas a top-cell bubble may depend on Omega_f^E, as Proposition 6.3 and Theorem 2.3 explicitly say. Section 9 repeats 'any space dimension'.
checks.limits: The current review does not silently strengthen local dependence to a single top cell, impose homogeneous physical boundary traces, or add an unstated n>=2 hypothesis.

checks.claim: The stated shape-regularity-only uniform L2 bound fails for the actual W^0 operator in dimension one.
proof: Use the fixed Lipschitz domain Omega=(0,1) with two intervals T0=[0,epsilon] and T1=[epsilon,1], where 0<epsilon<1/2. Every interval has diam(B_T)=diam(T), so c_T=1 for this entire family. The shared vertex patch has diameter ratio (1-epsilon)/epsilon, already disproving the local quasi-uniformity assertion (8.1) in Lemma 8.2 for n=1.

Equations (2.12)-(2.13) specify z_T=|T|^-1 dx on a top-dimensional interval and z_v=(1/deg(v))*sum_(T incident v) z_T at a vertex. This is the arithmetic average of the normalized interval densities, not a volume-weighted average over the union.

The paragraph on PDF15 gives z_(v,empty)=-z_v. The definition below (2.23) gives W^k=(-1)^(k-1)*sum_e phi_e integral(u wedge z_(e,empty)). At k=0 the two minus signs cancel and phi_v=lambda_v, hence W^0u=sum_v lambda_v integral(u z_v).

Choose u_epsilon(x)=6(x/epsilon)(1-x/epsilon) for 0<=x<=epsilon, and zero on the other interval. This is a continuous piecewise quadratic, smooth on each closed cell, with single-valued traces and zero physical endpoint values; thus it lies in the stated domain and in P_2 Lambda^0(T). Its small-cell average is 1, so the three nodal averaging coefficients of W^0u are exactly (1,1/2,0).

Therefore W^0u=1-x/(2epsilon) on [0,epsilon] and W^0u=(1-x)/(2(1-epsilon)) on [epsilon,1]. Direct integration gives ||u||_2^2=6epsilon/5, ||W^0u||_2^2=(1+6epsilon)/12, and ratio squared 5(1+6epsilon)/(72epsilon). Even the large interval alone gives ratio squared at least 5(1-epsilon)/(72epsilon). These tend to infinity while n=1, polynomial degree r=2, domain, and shape constant remain fixed.

The new reviewer-authored exact Fraction calculation independently integrates these three polynomials, obtaining reference squared integrals 6/5,7/12,1/12 and exact rational examples. The analytic formula, not merely the two numerical parameter choices, proves unboundedness.

The same mechanism can occur in nested one-dimensional refinements: retain [1/2,1] and repeatedly bisect the adjacent left cell toward 1/2, placing the zero-endpoint quadratic on the shrinking cell. Its average contributes 1/2 at the shared vertex and creates a fixed-sized output on [1/2,1], while its input norm squared is proportional to the shrinking length. Thus the issue is not an artifact of choosing a nonnested family.
checks.impact: This refutes Proposition 8.1 and Lemma 8.4 as stated with constants depending only on c_T and n, and hence the corresponding uniform-stability portion of Theorem 2.3 and its all-dimension formulation. It is a counterexample to a claimed bound for the defined operator, not just a gap in the proof of Lemma 8.2.
counterevidence_and_limits: The counterexample does not refute the algebraic decomposition, commutation, space preservation, or boundedness on each individual fixed mesh with a mesh-dependent constant.
It does not establish a failure in dimensions n>=2, where conforming shape-regular simplices have the relevant local comparability.
It does not identify a dependence on increasing polynomial degree: degree2 already suffices.
The input has zero values at both ends of the physical domain, so the failure cannot be removed merely by requiring those homogeneous scalar traces.
checks.repair: Restrict the shape-regularity-only statement to n>=2, or impose an explicit local adjacent-size comparability condition for n=1 and let constants depend on that bound. Altering the averaging weights would require a separate analysis of the construction and is not claimed as an already verified repair.

checks.claim: The overlap counting is sound, and the geometric obstruction in L02 is specifically the one-dimensional size comparison.
checks.reasoning: A fixed n-simplex T belongs to Omega_f precisely for its faces f. At a fixed dimension m this gives binom(n+1,m+1) overlaps, and over all nonempty faces it gives 2^(n+1)-1. For extended patches, membership means that f contains a vertex of T, so a bound on vertex-star cardinality bounds their overlap. Shape regularity bounds the solid-angle size below and hence the number of incident simplices for fixed n>=2. In a conforming Lipschitz vertex star, a facet-adjacency path connects its cells; when n>=2, a shared facet contains an edge, and shape regularity compares its length with the diameters on both sides. A uniformly bounded number of such steps gives local diameter comparability. In n=1 a common facet is only a point, so that argument supplies no length comparison, exactly as the explicit interval family shows.
checks.limits: The n=1 extended overlap itself is still bounded; it is the local quasi-uniformity component of Lemma 8.2 that fails. No global quasi-uniformity assumption is needed for the positive local argument in n>=2.

checks.claim: The uniformly bounded Whitney-coefficient argument introduces no hidden mesh-length or polynomial-degree parameter.
checks.reasoning: The recursive coefficient systems use incidence matrices with entries 0,1,-1 and a number of unknowns controlled by local simplex counts. Local exactness plus the imposed adjoint condition gives uniqueness on the relevant coefficient space. Consequently only finitely many matrix patterns occur for bounded size, and their inverse norms on the uniquely solvable subspace have a finite maximum. More explicitly, select a full-column-rank square minor: its nonzero integer determinant has absolute value at least1, and its cofactors are bounded by Hadamard's inequality in terms of the bounded dimension. Cramer's rule then bounds the coefficient infinity norm by a constant times the right-hand-side infinity norm. The induction (8.5)-(8.6) has bounded length at fixed n. The initial normalized top-cell volume form is plus or minus its normalized Whitney n-form, with coefficient of magnitude1.
checks.counterevidence: The coefficient bound itself can hold even on the nonuniform interval counterexample. What fails there is converting bounded coefficients into an L-infinity estimate with a single maximum patch diameter: a normalized Whitney one-form on a short interval is of size1/epsilon. Thus this valid algebraic argument does not rescue the missing geometric hypothesis.
checks.limits: Core owns the full local exactness and recursive-construction proofs. This check validates the uniform-bound inference from those properties; it does not relabel the entire core proof as reread here.

checks.claim: The apparent rho denominator in (8.2)-(8.3) is controlled by the barycentric numerator and the local mesh scale.
checks.reasoning: For e in f* and g a face of f, the vertex sets of e and g are disjoint. On any contributing simplex, rho_g=1-sum_(i in g)lambda_i is at least sum_(i in e)lambda_i. A Whitney j-form is a sum of terms lambda_i times j barycentric differentials. Under local diameter comparability and shape regularity, each d lambda has size O(h^-1). Hence dividing phi_e by rho_g leaves a bound O(h^-j). Uniformly bounded coefficient expansions give the same estimate for psi_(e,g)(f)/rho_g, and give ||mu_e||_infinity=O(h^(-j+1)). This is the structural cancellation required by (8.2)-(8.3), not a bound on rho_g^-1 in isolation.
checks.limits: At the set rho_g=0 the individual quotient is interpreted through its bounded almost-everywhere behavior for this norm estimate; smoothness of the assembled bubbles is established separately in the parent/core sections. The local comparability condition is essential, as L02 demonstrates.

checks.claim: The powers of h and b in the averaging, R, and Q terms cancel consistently once the geometric hypotheses for the local estimates hold.
checks.reasoning: In Pi_j G_f^*u, each of the j physical-y derivative slots contributes b because D_y G_f=b I. Thus b^-j cancels that factor before evaluation at L_g. The remaining k-j parameter derivatives contribute factors of length O(h), canceled by the O(h^-1) barycentric derivatives in the pullback L_g^*. The integration scale is h^n times the L-infinity norm of the weight, consistent with Lemma8.5. For an R term, ||z_(e,f)||_infinity=O(h^(j-n)) gives an averaged-form bound O(h^j); multiplication by (phi_e+psi_(e,g))/rho_g=O(h^-j) makes the overall bound dimensionless. For a Q term, Q_(e,f) uses Pi_(j+1) and a weight w_(e,f) of degree n-j-1 with size O(h^(j+1-n)). Rewrite its coefficient as rho_g^(j+1)*d(phi_e/rho_g^(j+1))=d phi_e-(j+1)d rho_g wedge(phi_e/rho_g). This has size O(h^(-j-1)); Lemma8.5 with index j+1 supplies O(h^(j+1)), again canceling. The A term is the j=0 case with an n-form weight of size O(h^-n).
checks.edge_cases: R vanishes for j>k; Q vanishes when j+1>k, consistent with their target form degrees. When g is empty, the pullback to a point kills positive-degree forms; the remaining scalar integral has no b singularity because b(0)=1.
checks.limits: The full kernel/Hardy estimate quoted as (8.11) of prior paper [7] in Lemma8.5 was not independently reconstructed or fully reread. This check verifies the cancellation, degree, and scaling of every type of term, conditional on that expressly imported local averaging bound and the required geometry.

checks.claim: The proof of Lemma8.4 has the correct scale cancellation and overlap structure when incident cell sizes are comparable.
checks.reasoning: With z_(e,empty) supported on Omega_e^E, bounded coefficients and comparable local sizes give ||z_(e,empty)||_infinity <=C h_e^(k-n). Cauchy-Schwarz yields |integral u wedge z_(e,empty)| <=C h_e^(k-n/2)||u||_(L2(Omega_e^E)). The Whitney basis form satisfies ||phi_e||_(L2(Omega_e)) <=C h_e^(n/2-k). The powers cancel. Pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz over the bounded number of active phi_e, followed by bounded extended-patch overlap, gives the global estimate. For f=empty the usable scale is h_e of its support, as used in the displayed proof, rather than an undefined maximum over an empty extended patch.
checks.limits: This is a conditional verification of the proof mechanism, not an assertion that Lemma8.4 holds in the unqualified n=1 scope. The exact violation of that scope is L02.

checks.claim: Once the local operator bounds hold, finite overlap yields the squared stable sum including the top-cell bubbles.
checks.reasoning: For each f, the number of g subfaces, j values, and e simplices in its link is uniformly bounded by n and the shape-controlled local incidence count. Therefore 'finitely many terms' in the proof can be strengthened to a uniform count; it does not grow with the global number of mesh cells or with r. Summing the local K bounds over proper faces uses the fixed-dimensional macroelement overlap. For proper-face bubbles, B_f=K_(m,f)+K_(m+1,f) gives an immediate squared-norm bound. For a top cell T, (2.26) gives B_T=u|_T-Wu|_T-sum_(g proper face of T)B_g|_T. There are only finitely many such faces depending on n; squaring, integrating, and summing over top cells controls these residual bubbles by ||u||^2+||Wu||^2+sum_g||B_g||^2. The extended input patch in Proposition6.3 is needed for the W contribution and is explicitly retained.
checks.limits: These deductions inherit the qualification on the local bounds; they cannot remove the W^0 counterexample in L02. They do not require treating the top-cell operator as depending only on u|_T.

checks.claim: L2 boundedness plus commutation gives the stated graph-norm stability in the scope where the L2 estimates hold.
checks.reasoning: Piecewise smooth conforming forms contain smooth compactly supported forms and are dense in L2, so a proved L2 bound yields a unique bounded extension. The support and domain-of-dependence properties pass through L2 limits. For H Lambda^k, use graph-norm approximation and the closedness of the exterior derivative: dB_f^k u=B_f^(k+1)du and dW^k u=W^(k+1)du persist. Summing the degree-k L2 bound and the degree-(k+1) bound applied to du gives ||W^k u||_(H Lambda^k)^2+sum_f||B_f^k u||_(H Lambda^k)^2 <=C(||u||_2^2+||du||_2^2). For k=n the derivative term is zero; for k=0 this is H1, and in n=3 the intermediate graph spaces are H(curl) and H(div).
checks.limits: Boundary traces are those in the source's conforming spaces. The theorem does not by itself assert preservation of every separately imposed homogeneous boundary subspace. The present counterexample has homogeneous scalar endpoint values but the resulting bound failure concerns L2, independently of graph-norm extension.

checks.claim: The intended degree-independent conclusion follows from ambient-space bounds and invariance, with the geometric qualification made explicit.
checks.reasoning: The operators are defined from the mesh, finite-degree weight forms, pullbacks and averaging, not from a selected polynomial degree r. The constants in the checked estimates depend on fixed n, incidence counts and geometric regularity, and no polynomial inverse inequality containing r is used. Consequently, when those bounds hold, restricting the same operators to the invariant global-degree spaces P_r Lambda^k and P_r^- Lambda^k gives the same constant for all r>=1. Form-degree edge cases are handled by the zero maps in L06 and by d=0 above degree n. Boundary stars have fewer incident cells; no new scaling singularity appears merely from being a boundary face. The interval counterexample shows that local size comparability still has to be stated correctly.
checks.limits: The explicitly stated invariance concerns the displayed P_r and P_r^- spaces. An arbitrary independently assigned degree on each individual cell is not automatically covered by global-degree invariance alone; no additional variable-degree preservation theorem is inferred here. The n=1 counterexample already fixes r=2, so it does not undermine the separate absence of r in the valid conditional estimates.

checks.claim: The claimed refinement of the earlier bubble transform and the stated preconditioner consequences are distinguished from reproduced computations.
checks.reasoning: The article identifies its new feature as preservation by each individual local bubble, whereas it attributes only grouped preservation to the prior rational-bubble construction. Section9 explains the alternative chain/averaging construction even for zero-forms and contrasts it with extension and sequential procedures. It points to an established mixed Hodge-Laplace preconditioning framework rather than supplying a benchmark implementation. The present checks preserve that attribution and the stronger local-space-preserving goal.
checks.limits: The prior papers [2],[4],[6]-[9],[12] were not separately fully read by this helper. No priority claim, full reproduction of prior methods, numerical preconditioner experiment, or condition-number benchmark is asserted. Missing optional code is not a mathematical defect. The all-dimension uniform stability language in Section9 must reflect L02.

findings.title: Shape regularity alone does not give the stated uniform stability in dimension one
